_comment: Shared topography lookup + coarse-organ -> ICD-O-3 C-code crosswalk consulted by site_capture, presentation_router.site_to_group and dual_group_rules, and the output block (Architecture & File System §4C). Labels drawn from the RedCap topography drop-down (RedCap Options/Topography Redcap.md); redcap_code is that file's 3-digit dropdown value (drop the 'C' and the decimal point).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 1's Ia4 dual-group rule for 9591 turns on exactly the C42.2-vs-rest distinction, so these four codes are individually addressable below, never lumped as C42.x.
coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Blood, bone marrow and haematopoietic system
coarse_organ_crosswalk.region_hint: Every leukaemia except myeloid sarcoma is recorded at C42.1 Bone marrow, wherever the blasts were seen (WHO ICD-O-3 Rule E). Pick C42.2 Spleen only for a lymphoma that arose in the spleen; a myeloid sarcoma is recorded at the organ it arose in.
coarse_organ_crosswalk.region_question: Which of these does the disease arise in?

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Peripheral nerves and autonomic nervous system
Connective, subcutaneous and other soft tissues
Skin
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Kaposi sarcoma of the skin is the one soft tissue sarcoma Visser 2023 Table 3 registers at basis 1, at C44 (Group 9 build contract §0.7). Topography Redcap.md offers no 444 (C44.4, skin of scalp and neck), so that code is not listed (registrar questions H2).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Urinary bladder
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Bladder and prostate are classic sites of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma in young children (ICCC-3 IXa at any site).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Prostate gland
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Prostatic rhabdomyosarcoma, ICCC-3 IXa at any site.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Vulva, vagina and cervix
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Botryoid embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of the vagina and cervix (ICCC-3 IXa); yolk sac tumour of the vagina is Group X; carcinoma is Group XI.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Uterus and placenta
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Added 6 October 2026 (Group 10 code review). Gestational trophoblastic tumours of the uterus and placenta are Group X (ICCC-2017 range 104, Xb5, sites 540-559 and 589); rhabdomyosarcoma is Group IX; carcinoma is Group XI.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Epididymis, spermatic cord and scrotum
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Paratesticular rhabdomyosarcoma, ICCC-3 IXa at any site. The testis itself (C62) stays in the gonad row.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Extrahepatic bile duct and biliary tract
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 9 added 2 October 2026 (Group 9 build contract §7.4). Botryoid embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of the bile ducts, ICCC-3 IXa. The liver and intrahepatic bile duct (C22) stay in the liver row.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Adrenal gland and paraspinal sympathetic chain
Brain, meninges and central nervous system
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group III keys its decision trees to anatomical COMPARTMENT, so this list must be the full C70-C72 set, not three NOS codes. The router picks the tree from the code chosen here and asks no further question, which makes region capture load-bearing for this group in a way it is not for the others. Expanded 2026-09-14 with the Group 3 build. C71.0 has no REDCap topography option (the dropdown jumps 709 to 711) — see docs/TODO.md.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Eye
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Expanded from C69.9 alone to all nine C69 codes, Group 5 build contract §7.1 -- without C69.2 (Retina), the topography Visser Table 3 names for retinoblastoma, a retina-sited retinoblastoma could not reach Group V at all. C69.4 (Ciliary body) alone carries an additional candidate group in topography_lookup -- [5, 4] -- because intraocular medulloepithelioma at that site is an ICCC-3 Group IV tumour and a genuine leukocoria mimic (contract §5.3). Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma (Group 9) and ocular melanoma (Group 11) also arise at C69 and belong in the relevant per-code candidate_groups once those groups are built; not added now. C69.6 orbit also lists Group 9 (orbital rhabdomyosarcoma).
Craniopharyngeal duct and pineal gland -- consulted by the 8000-8005 (NOS) dual-group rule (DT master §6) alongside C70-C72 and C75.1.
coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Craniopharyngeal duct and pineal gland
Nasopharynx
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 4's sinonasal tree (g4_sinonasal) claims this block for the olfactory-neuroblastoma / sinonasal differential (Group 4 build contract §5). Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (ICCC-3 XId) is the dominant paediatric malignancy at this site in older children, so group 11 is listed too.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Nasal cavity and middle ear
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: C30.0 is the site ICD-O-3.2 itself prints against 9522/3 Olfactory neuroblastoma; C30.1 is 8690's own site (Middle ear paraganglioma). Both are also classic parameningeal sites for embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (group 9).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Accessory sinuses
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Kadish B/C olfactory neuroblastoma extends into the paranasal sinuses (group 4); the sinuses are also a classic parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma site (group 9).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Mediastinum
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 4's sympathoadrenal tree (g4_sympathoadrenal) includes the mediastinum for posterior mediastinal/paraspinal neuroblastoma; an anterior mediastinal mass in a child is more commonly lymphoma (group 2). The compartment alone does not decide, so both groups are listed.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Lung and bronchus
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Added 7 October 2026 (audit of Group X, F-A-05). ICD-O-3.2 codes an immature teratoma of the lung, thymus or thyroid 9080/1 and elsewhere 9080/3, so the site has to be recordable for Group X to record the pair. ICCC-2017 holds carcinomas of this organ in Group XI (XIf4, carcinomas of lung), which is not built; Group 11 is listed so the family question is complete when it is.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Thymus
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Added 7 October 2026 (audit of Group X, F-A-05). ICD-O-3.2 codes an immature teratoma of the lung, thymus or thyroid 9080/1 and elsewhere 9080/3, so the site has to be recordable for Group X to record the pair. ICCC-2017 holds carcinomas of this organ in Group XI (XIf5, carcinomas of thymus), which is not built; Group 11 is listed so the family question is complete when it is.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Thyroid gland
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Added 7 October 2026 (audit of Group X, F-A-05). ICD-O-3.2 codes an immature teratoma of the lung, thymus or thyroid 9080/1 and elsewhere 9080/3, so the site has to be recordable for Group X to record the pair. ICCC-2017 holds carcinomas of this organ in Group XI (XIb, thyroid carcinomas), which is not built; Group 11 is listed so the family question is complete when it is.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Lip, tongue, gum, floor of mouth, palate and cheek
Heart, pleura and other thoracic sites
Fallopian tube, ligaments and other female genital organs
Ill-defined sites
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: WHO ICD-O-3 Rule B and Rule A: a region, or a prefixed region (peri-, para-, area of), that the report gives with no tissue is recorded at the ill-defined subcategory. Offered after the organ systems; candidate_groups is route_by_morphology, so the presentation's own list decides the family. C76.3 Pelvis, NOS is offered under Ovary, testis and sacrococcygeal region, where Group 10 placed it (design decision D19), so it is not listed twice.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Unknown primary site
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: WHO ICD-O-3 Rule D: a lymphoma with no site indicated and an extranodal origin suspected is recorded at C80.9.
